Automate Verse with n8n#

Status: the n8n-nodes-verse package type-checks and builds, its manifest and webhook-signature check are verified — it is **not yet published** to npm or n8n's verified community nodes. Until it is, install it from integrations/automation/n8n/ in the repo (npm link) or from a tarball on a self-hosted n8n.

n8n is the self-hosted option: a workflow waits for a scene to finish or a comment to land, then does whatever its 400-odd other nodes do — Slack, mail, sheets, your CRM. Going the other way, it can hand Verse a file link, or the bytes of a file it already holds, and get a scene back.

You need: a Verse account token (see Share privately with tokens) and an n8n instance (self-hosted, or cloud once the package is verified).

1. Install and connect#

Self-hosted: Settings → Community nodes → Install n8n-nodes-verse (after it is on npm), or npm link the folder into ~/.n8n/nodes. Then create a Verse Engine API credential:

  • Verse Server — the origin your account lives on (prefilled with the public host; self-hosters paste their own).
  • Account Token — the 64-hex token from POST /v1/account or /studio.

The credential test calls GET /v1/account.

2. Nodes#

NodeResource · operationWhat it does
Verse Engine Triggerevents: Scene Ready, Scene Failed, Comment Added, Version Promoted, Configuration ChangedRegisters a webhook on your account when the workflow is activated and removes it on deactivation. Each delivery is checked against the hook's secret (X-Verse-Signature) before the workflow runs. Output: id, event, t, account and the event's fields (job, url, scene, comment, …).
Verse Enginescene · ListEvery scene you own with link, visibility, stats, open review count.
scene · Get AnalyticsViews, unique viewers, time spent, funnel, rooms over 7, 30 or 90 days.
scene · Create Share LinkMints a tokened link (shareUrl) — what opens a private scene.
scene · Set Visibilitypublic, unlisted or private.
upload · From URLHands Verse a public file link; returns job and the share link it will have.
upload · From Binary FileSends the item's binary bytes to POST /v1/ingest — for files n8n already fetched (a Read Binary File, HTTP Request or Dropbox download node before it).

3. Worked example: new scene → Slack#

  1. Verse Engine Trigger, events Scene Ready.
  2. Slack → Send a message. Text:
    Code
    New scene ready: {{ $json.job }}
{{ $json.url }}
  3. Activate the workflow. n8n registers the webhook; the next upload you own posts its link the moment the compile finishes. Deactivating deletes the webhook.

4. Worked example: Dropbox file → Verse scene#

Two ways, pick one:

  • By link — Dropbox Trigger (new file) → **Dropbox → Get a shared link → Verse Engine → upload · From URL** with that link (dl=1) and the file name as Scene Name.
  • By bytes — Dropbox Trigger → Dropbox → Download → **Verse Engine → upload · From Binary File** (binary property data). No public link is needed; the file goes from n8n straight to Verse, under the same 512 MB cap.

Either returns job; the scene is live when the trigger fires scene.ready for it, or when GET /v1/ingest/<job> says status: done. Uploads count against your account's ingest rate (20 per hour per token).

The same thing over HTTP#

Every operation is a documented call, so an HTTP Request node with the bearer header does the same while the package is unlisted: subscribe with POST /v1/account/webhooks, upload with POST /v1/ingest/url { "url": "https://…/model.glb", "name": "flat" }, mint a link with POST /v1/scenes/<id>/share. Verify deliveries the way the webhook section shows.
